_note: Extra visitor content per destination id, shown on Destination Details. Provisional, like the register: check against the businesses before release. Avoid prices and opening hours here; they change.

grand-turk-cruise-center.tagline: Your ship, a lagoon pool and a white-sand beach in one place
highlights: A huge lagoon-style pool with cabanas and a bridge, right beside the pier
The Cruise Center beach, one of the nicest port beaches in the region
Duty-free shops, art galleries, jewellers and souvenir stalls
A FlowRider surf simulator for stand-up surfing and bodyboarding
tips: The complex opened in 2006 and covers about 13 acres, so allow time to walk back to the gangway
Governor's Beach is under 1 km north, but you can't walk there along the sand; use the inland road
Return to Ship in this app always brings you back here

john-glenn-exhibit.tagline: Where the space age splashed down
highlights: A Mercury rocket model standing tall over the plaza
A splashing-capsule sculpture under red-and-white canopies
A life-size astronaut figure, perfect for a photo
Information boards on Friendship 7 and the Mercury programme
tips: Only about 100 m from the ship: a good first or last stop
John Glenn was brought to Grand Turk for his debriefing after splashing down on 20 February 1962

jacks-shack.tagline: Colourful beach bar on the sand, a short walk from the ship
highlights: Rows of beach loungers and umbrellas on soft white sand
A bright, open-air bar and deck with sea views
Calm, clear water on Grand Turk's sheltered west coast
tips: About 1 km on foot from the ship: wear sun protection for the walk
Ask at the bar about loungers and umbrellas before you settle in

grand-turk-lighthouse.tagline: The 1852 cast-iron lighthouse at the island's northern tip
highlights: The white cast-iron tower, made in England and shipped out in sections
A shady park behind the white fence and the "Grand Turk" gate
Views over the reef and the Atlantic from the northern point
Wild donkeys often wander near the park
tips: It's about 11 km from the ship each way: most visitors take a taxi or a tour
Bring water: there is little shade on the road north

national-museum.tagline: The islands' story, from Taíno settlers to the space race
highlights: Guinep House, one of the oldest stone buildings on the island (before 1885)
The Molasses Reef wreck, from the early 1500s, one of the oldest known shipwrecks in the Americas
A colourful mosaic wall and a classic red telephone box outside
An arboretum with marked trails next door
tips: On Front Street, so it pairs well with St. Mary's and the Freemason Lodge
The museum opened in 1991

hm-prison.tagline: Walk through 160 years of island justice
highlights: The whitewashed walls and arched gate of the 1830s prison
Rooms staged to show prisoners' daily lives
The bell tower, which was rung five times a day
Donkey Bites snack bar and a gift shop inside the grounds
tips: The prison was in use until 1994
Self-guided with signs throughout; usually open when a ship is in port
Tickets and booking rules can change: check before you go

st-marys.tagline: A white church with red shutters, facing the sea
highlights: Gothic arched windows framed in bright red shutters
Its seafront setting on the Cockburn Town waterfront
Made a Pro-Cathedral of the Anglican diocese in the 1990s
tips: Originally built around 1900; St. Thomas Church (1823) nearby is older
Please dress modestly and keep quiet if a service is on

highlights: Bright blue shutters, doors and balcony rails under a red roof
The Masonic square-and-compasses emblem on the gable
Hand-cut limestone walls from the salt-raking era
tips: View from outside: lodge meetings are not open to the public
Best photographed from across the street in the morning light

clock-tower-park.tagline: A tidy green park with a tall clock tower and pergolas
highlights: The green Millennium Clock Tower with its bell
White pergolas with green roofs, and a bronze bust on a plinth
The "Welcome to Over Back" sign and the Turks and Caicos flag
tips: Traffic drives on the left here: look right first when crossing

town-salina.tagline: The salt ponds that built Grand Turk
highlights: A red-roofed gazebo with picnic benches right at the water's edge
Painted planters lining the pond wall
Wading birds feeding in the shallow, still water
Banners marking 50 years of ministerial government
tips: Salt raked from these ponds was once the island's main export
Early morning is calmest for reflections and birds

sand-bar.tagline: Waterfront bar and grill with a deck over the beach
highlights: A covered deck looking straight out over turquoise water
Right on the beach along the Duke Street waterfront
West-facing, so it's a great spot for late-afternoon light
tips: In Cockburn Town, about 4.5 km from the ship
Watch the time: leave plenty of margin to walk back for all-aboard

salt-raker-inn.tagline: A historic seaside inn with a garden restaurant
highlights: A turquoise two-storey house with a long upstairs veranda
Picket fence and garden seating facing the sea
A classic of Duke Street's Bermudian-style architecture
tips: Close to Sandbar and the museum: easy to combine

barbies.tagline: Local and Caribbean cooking with a covered terrace
highlights: Island dishes on a menu board at the door
A shaded wooden terrace with tables
Part of a small row of local shops
tips: Seats are for customers only, as the signs say

pillory-beach.tagline: Calm water and soft sand north of town
highlights: Gentle waves and clear turquoise water
Good snorkelling close to the shore
A long, uncrowded strip of white sand
tips: Renamed Guanahani Beach in 1992, after the Taíno name for Columbus's first landfall
Little shade: bring a hat, water and reef-safe sunscreen
Seaweed can wash up after windy days

cibc-bank.tagline: Bank branch with an ATM in Cockburn Town
highlights: ATM for cash withdrawals
Modern two-storey branch with parking in front
tips: The Turks and Caicos Islands use the US dollar
Many small vendors prefer cash

graceway-supermarket.tagline: Stock up on water, snacks and sunscreen
highlights: A full-service supermarket by the salt pond
Cold drinks, snacks and everyday essentials
Gracebay Pharmacy is in the same building
tips: Prices are in US dollars

highlights: Over-the-counter medicines and first aid
Sun care and after-sun products
tips: Bring any prescription with you
In an emergency, call 911

medical-centre.tagline: Grand Turk's hospital, with emergency care
highlights: Emergency department
Modern single- and two-storey buildings with a drop-off entrance
tips: In an emergency, call 911
Tell the ship's medical centre too, so they know where you are

police-station.tagline: Main police station on Grand Turk
highlights: The yellow "A" Division building
Help with lost property and reporting incidents
tips: In an emergency, call 911

governors-beach.tagline: Wide white sand and shade trees, close to the ship
highlights: Some of the island's clearest, calmest water
Casuarina trees for natural shade
Quieter than the Cruise Center beach
tips: Reach it by the inland road; you can't walk along the sand from the Cruise Center

cockburn-town.tagline: The capital, with colonial streets by the sea
highlights: Bermudian-style houses along Front Street and Duke Street
The National Museum, St. Mary's and the old prison within a short walk
Salt ponds and wading birds right behind the waterfront
tips: About 5 km from the ship: allow plenty of time to walk back
Traffic drives on the left: look right first when crossing

highlights: Old stone walls and shuttered houses from the salt-raking era
Sea views between the buildings
The museum and churches along the way

columbus-landfall.tagline: A protected marine park on the west coast
highlights: Clear water over the reef
Grand Turk is one of the places proposed as Columbus's first landfall in 1492
tips: Protected area: don't touch or take coral, shells or sea life

gibbs-cay.tagline: A tiny cay famous for friendly stingrays
highlights: Southern stingrays gliding in the shallows
A small, uninhabited island with clear water
tips: Only reachable by boat tour: book through your ship or a licensed operator

margaritaville.tagline: Big beach bar with a swim-up pool beside the ship
highlights: The largest Margaritaville in the Caribbean
A swim-up bar in the lagoon pool
tips: Open when a cruise ship is in port
